item.title: FIFA U17 WWC: Flamingos sail into semi finals, to meet Brazil
item.description: Nigeria’s Flamingos booked their place in the semi-finals of this year’s FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup finals after securing a 1-0 victory over Venezuela on Sunday night, with Azeezatt Oduntan scoring a late penalty in the 89th minute. The quarter-final contest had been closely fought, with Nigeria creating several opportunities but finding Venezuela goalkeeper Valeria Rebanales a huge stumbling block. The Flamingos enjoyed much of the attacking play in the first half, but Rebanales produced a couple of saves to keep the scores level. Midfielder Favour Nkwocha was also cautioned as Nigeria continued to press for an opening goal. Head Coach Hakeem Busari made his first change of the evening, introducing Precious Oscar for Oluwakemi Adegbuyi as Nigeria looked to find a way through. The deadlock remained unbroken until the 88th minute, when the referee initially awarded Nigeria a penalty before being invited to the VAR monitor to review the decision. Following the review, the penalty was upheld, and Oduntan stepped forward to convert from the spot with a minute left on the clock, giving Nigeria the breakthrough. Top scorer Oluebube Umejiaku had won the penalty for the Flamingos, setting up Oduntan to deliver the decisive moment of the contest. The victory sends Nigeria into the semi-finals, where they will face Brazil, who secured a 2-1 win over China in their quarter-final encounter. item.title: Nathaniel Bassey becomes first African gospel artist to hit one billion YouTube views
item.description: Nigerian gospel singer and pastor Nathaniel Bassey has surpassed one billion views on YouTube, becoming the first African gospel artist to achieve the milestone. Bassey’s official YouTube channel, Nathaniel Bassey Main, has amassed more than 1.014 billion views and 5.24 million subscribers since its creation in 2011, according to figures displayed on the platform at the time of filing this report. The achievement coincides with the October 2026 edition of the Hallelujah Challenge, the online prayer and worship programme founded by the gospel minister in 2017. The monthly initiative features midnight sessions of praise, worship and prayers, attracting participants from different parts of the world. Initially launched as an online worship gathering, the Hallelujah Challenge has grown into an international Christian movement, with thousands of people participating in its live sessions and millions more watching recorded editions. Bassey is known for popular gospel songs such as Imela , Onise Iyanu , Olowogbogboro and You Are God , which have contributed to his popularity among gospel music audiences in Nigeria and beyond. The one-billion-view milestone has generated excitement among his followers, with some suggesting that the minister could explore opportunities to monetise the growing audience of his online worship sessions. However, Bassey has maintained that the Hallelujah Challenge is primarily focused on worship and spiritual devotion rather than revenue generation. item.title: Catholic Diocese disowns Enugu APC campaign council list
item.description: …Bishop Obodo demands removal of his name, warns of legal action By Anayo Okoli The Catholic Diocese of Enugu has disowned the inclusion of the Auxiliary Bishop of Enugu, Most Rev. Ernest Anezichukwu Obodo, in the Enugu State All Progressives Congress, APC, Campaign Council, saying he was listed without his knowledge or consent. The Diocese also demanded the immediate removal of the bishop’s name and those of other Catholic priests allegedly included in the campaign council without their authorisation. Obodo, who is also the Enugu State Chairman of the Christian Association of Nigeria, CAN, was reportedly named Director of the Faith-Based Campaign Group in the APC campaign council. In a disclaimer dated October 30, 2026, and signed by the Diocesan Chancellor and Secretary, Very Rev. Fr. Wilfred Chidi Agubuchie, the Diocese described the inclusion as unauthorised, misleading and a misrepresentation of the bishop’s political disposition. The statement said the action was a “malicious act of misrepresentation and defamation,” adding that it undermined the bishop’s integrity and ecclesiastical reputation. “The Catholic Diocese of Enugu has become aware of reports concerning the inclusion of the name of Most Rev. Ernest Anezichukwu Obodo, Auxiliary Bishop of Enugu and Chairman of the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN), Enugu State, as Director of the Faith-Based Campaign Group in the Enugu State APC Campaign Council, alongside the names of some Catholic priests. “We categorically state that the inclusion of the Bishop’s name without his knowledge or consent is wholly unauthorised, misleading and unacceptable,” the statement said. The Diocese stressed that the Catholic Church did not engage in partisan politics, participate in political campaigns or endorse political parties. It said the Church remained politically neutral and committed to its spiritual mission and the promotion of peace, justice and the common good. While acknowledging the right of individual Christians to participate in civic and democratic activities, the Diocese warned against using the name, office or identity of the Church and its ministers for partisan political interests. “We therefore demand the immediate removal of Bishop Ernest Obodo’s name, as well as the names of all other Catholic priests included without their knowledge and consent, from the said campaign list and any related publications,” it said. The Diocese further warned that any continued or subsequent unauthorised use of the bishop’s name, title, image or ecclesiastical office for partisan political purposes would attract appropriate legal action. “For the avoidance of doubt, the Catholic Church is not a political campaign organisation and must not be presented as one,” the statement added. item.description: Gov. Chukwuma Soludo of Anambra has urged South-East political leaders to abandon opposition politics and embrace greater integration with the Federal Government. Soludo made the call at a stakeholders’ meeting on Sunday in Awka. The meeting had political leaders and grassroots mobilisers from the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), All Progressives Congress (APC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and Accord Party. According to him, the era of opposition politics, which became prominent in the South-East during the 2015 general elections, should give way to active participation in governance at the centre. He said that considerable work was required at the grassroots to change public perception of the government and mobilise support for the president. item.description: Threatens arrest for anyone obstructing rival parties By Steve Oko & Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has warned Labour Party supporters against disrupting the campaign activities of opposition parties ahead of the 2027 general elections, declaring that he has not authorised anyone to interfere with their democratic rights. item.title: NDC chieftain tackles Kalu over Obi’s four-year presidency proposal
item.description: By Anayo Okoli ENUGU — A chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Barrister Peter Agubuzu, has faulted the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, over his criticism of a proposal for the South-East to accept a single four-year presidential term. Agubuzu described Kalu’s remarks as misplaced, urging him to focus on addressing the economic hardship and rising cost of living confronting Nigerians rather than dwelling on how long the South-East might wait to produce a President. Kalu had reportedly criticised South-East stakeholders advocating a single four-year presidential term for the region, an arrangement attributed to the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi. Speaking at an All Progressives Congress (APC) women’s rally in Enugu on Saturday, the Deputy Speaker reportedly said the Igbo could not afford to wait 60 years to produce a President who would serve for only four years. Reacting, Agubuzu, a senior lawyer, said the immediate concern of Nigerians was the worsening economic situation and the need for leadership capable of addressing the country’s challenges. He argued that Obi’s proposal was driven by the need to transform Nigeria’s economy from consumption to production and lift millions of citizens out of poverty. “While Nigerians across the country are chanting ‘Tinubu Must Go’ because of the economic hardship they are experiencing and their fear of a worsening economic crisis if Tinubu is re-elected, our brother, the Deputy Speaker, is talking about 60 years. “He forgot that Obi’s primary objective is to transform Nigeria from consumption to production to lift millions out of poverty. This is why Nigerians are chanting Tinubu Must Go,” Agubuzu said. He maintained that the major concern of Obi was how to address the country’s economic difficulties and restore hope to millions of Nigerians struggling with the rising cost of living. “What Nigerians are saying is straightforward: Peter Obi should come and salvage the country from the impending economic disaster they fear will follow if President Tinubu is re-elected. “Nigerians are worried about their survival, their livelihoods and the future of their children. That is the urgent issue before us, not a speculative debate about waiting 60 years for an Igbo President,” he said. The NDC chieftain further argued that discussions about a single presidential term should be considered within the broader context of national unity, equity and political inclusion. He urged political leaders to pay greater attention to the concerns of ordinary Nigerians and focus on practical solutions to the country’s economic challenges rather than allow debates over regional claims to the presidency to overshadow demands for effective leadership. Mustapha Habu Ringim, ENGAUSA GLOBAL TECH HUB LTD has consistently demonstrated this philosophy through its innovative, multilingual and inclusive approach to technology education, skills development, entrepreneurship and human capital development. Other important Federal Government stakeholders include the Industrial Training Fund (ITF) and the National Directorate of Employment (NDE). I will soon dedicate separate blog posts to celebrating the contributions of each of these key stakeholders, as well as other partners from both the public and private sectors. Our impactful relationship with NITDA, particularly in advancing digital inclusion, dates back to 2020, when the Agency recognised the grassroots impact of ENGAUSA’s digital inclusion programmes and incentivised our innovation hub with computers. This support was subsequently extended through the provision of smartphone repair tools, partnering in the national and local training programs and graduation ceremonies, further strengthening our capacity to deliver practical, industry-relevant training. Beyond these material contributions, NITDA’s confidence in ENGAUSA®’s experience and grassroots impact has also been reflected in the Agency’s repeated engagement of our Hub in policy development and strategic framework review processes. We have participated in several stakeholder consultations and workshops relating to key national initiatives, including the Nigeria Startup Policy, the National Digital Literacy Framework (NDLF) and the Three Million Technical Talent (3MTT) programme. These engagements have provided opportunities for ENGAUSA® to contribute practical insights from its experience in inclusive digital skills development, grassroots innovation, entrepreneurship and human capital development. The results speak for themselves. ENGAUSA’s six-year impact journey has contributed to reaching over 11,000 beneficiaries, creating more than 12,000 direct and indirect jobs, and supporting the establishment and growth of over 1,000 startup businesses, SMEs and freelance enterprises across 22 states of Nigeria. 2022 Graduation Ceremony of 1,353 ENGAUSA® Trainees, Delivered in Collaboration with NITDA. NITDA has recognised these contributions through two major national recognitions within four years. The first was the Best Trainer of the Year Award in 2022, presented during the Digital Nigeria Conference. The second was the recent special recognition award presented during the Digital Literacy Workshop organised by NITDA on 20 October 2026, in recognition of ENGAUSA®’s outstanding contributions to digital inclusion and employment among the 252 Digital Literacy Centres registered on NITDA’s National Digital Literacy Dashboard. These recognitions affirm the importance of sustained institutional support for organisations delivering measurable impact at the grassroots. One of the most important lessons from our nearly seven years of programme implementation and impact assessment is that language inclusion is far more than a teaching technique. It is a powerful instrument for breaking barriers to education, technology and economic participation. By using Hausa alongside English in our learning environment, ENGAUSA has demonstrated that people should not be denied access to technical knowledge simply because they are not proficient in the dominant language of instruction. This approach has helped expand inclusion across several dimensions, including disability, gender, age, culture, education, economic circumstances and geographical location. It has created more accessible learning opportunities for persons with physical, sensory and other educational support needs; expanded opportunities for women and girls to acquire technical and entrepreneurial skills; and brought children, young people and adults into shared learning environments. It has also enabled learners from diverse cultural and traditional backgrounds to participate confidently while opening pathways for Almajiris, out-of-school children and young people, school dropouts and people with little or no formal educational qualifications. By reducing the cost barriers to acquiring employable and entrepreneurial skills and extending opportunities beyond conventional urban and formal educational environments, the approach has made skills development more accessible to underserved communities. Our experience also reinforces an important policy position: language-related barriers deserve explicit recognition as educational accessibility concerns. While language disadvantage is not itself a disability, it can prevent learners, including persons with disabilities, from understanding, communicating and participating fully in education and skills development. No learner should be left behind because of language or disability. The ENGAUSA experience has also contributed to changing perceptions about the value of technical competencies. Through competency-based training, recognition of prior learning, practical mentoring and enterprise incubation, we have promoted the dignity of skills and the formalisation of informal businesses. Our programmes have opened doors for people with zero certificates, Almajiris, unemployed and underemployed university graduates, women, freelancers and online workers. Many have progressed from learners to competent technicians, independent service providers, business owners and employers of labour. Some graduates have gone further to become multipliers of opportunity, reaching thousands of other beneficiaries through their own training, mentoring, business activities and community engagements. More than 11,000 people have benefited from ENGAUSA®’s highly subsidised skills acquisition programmes and 100% scholarship opportunities supported by partner organisations and individual philanthropists. Perhaps one of our most remarkable achievements is the creation of learning environments where people from different educational, socioeconomic, religious, traditional and cultural backgrounds sit together, learn together and build their futures without stereotypes or discrimination. item.description: Former Kogi West senator, Dino Melaye, has accused the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) of taking steps to rig the 2027 general elections, warning that any attempt to manipulate the polls would be resisted. Melaye made the allegation in a post on his X handle on Sunday, claiming that recent activities by the electoral body suggest what he described as “anticipatory rigging”. “The activities of INEC in recent times point at anticipatory rigging. Which will be resisted,” Melaye wrote. His comments come amid controversy over the discovery of AI-generated photographs in INEC’s preliminary voters’ register, as well as complaints by political parties over the omission of some candidates from the commission’s final list. item.title: 2027: ADC-PCC challenges Tinubu to defend failure to deliver electricity
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has challenged President Bola Tinubu to account for his failure to deliver on his 2023 electricity pledge, insisting that he should not seek re-election without fulfilling the promise. The council said Nigerians had not forgotten Tinubu’s categorical declaration during the 2023 presidential campaign that they should not vote for him for a second term if he failed to deliver electricity, dismissing attempts by the APC to reinterpret his words as an afterthought. In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC was reacting to comments by Dele Alake, spokesperson of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, defending the President’s electricity record. “Don’t vote for me for second term if I fail to deliver electricity,” the President had told Nigerians during the 2023 campaign. The opposition campaign council argued that more than three years after the pledge, Nigerians were still grappling with persistent power outages, repeated national grid collapses and inadequate electricity supply. It accused the Tinubu administration of increasing the financial burden on consumers through higher electricity bills, discriminatory tariff classifications and continued estimated billing, despite the much-publicised Presidential Metering Initiative. The council also said businesses, including hotels and other hospitality facilities, had resorted to rationing electricity by switching off power for guests during daytime hours to reduce operating costs. Dismissing the administration’s reliance on the Electricity Act and bond programmes to defend its record, the ADC-PCC insisted that policy documents and financial instruments could not substitute for actual electricity supply. “An Act is not electricity. A bond prospectus does not power homes and factories. Nigerians cannot eat statutes. What Nigerians need is electricity that works, not another round of explanations and publicity,” the council said. It further accused the administration of imposing higher tariffs without ensuring reliable supply, leaving households, manufacturers and small businesses to contend with rising operating costs. The ADC-PCC also questioned the implementation of the Presidential Metering Initiative, alleging that electricity distribution companies continued to impose estimated bills on consumers. “The President’s own condition for seeking a second term was straightforward: deliver electricity or do not ask Nigerians for another mandate,” the council maintained. It urged the APC to address the President’s 2023 commitment directly, rather than attempt to dilute his words, warning that the administration’s electricity record would be a major issue as Nigerians prepare to decide whether to renew Tinubu’s mandate in the January 16, 2027 election. item.title: APM Members Defect To PDP In Katsina, Back Danmarke’s Governorship Bid
item.description: At least 5,000 members of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) in Katsina State have reportedly joined the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), pledging support for the party’s governorship candidate, Senator Yakubu Lado Danmarke, ahead of the 2027 elections. The defectors, led by the Chairman of Katsina Frontiers, Alhaji Aliyu Sani, formally joined the PDP at a rally in Katsina on Sunday. Sani said the decision followed the group’s confidence in Danmarke’s leadership qualities and record of humanitarian support, particularly for the poor, vulnerable, elderly and children. He cited the senator’s provision of food and cash assistance, especially during Ramadan, describing him as a humble and compassionate leader who puts the welfare of the people above personal comfort and material wealth. Also speaking at the rally, Muhammad Hassan El-Makki said Katsina needed a leader genuinely committed to the well-being of its people. He described Danmarke as experienced and capable of transforming agriculture, healthcare, energy and infrastructure, while pointing to his scholarship programmes and contributions to community development. El-Makki urged residents to support the senator’s governorship ambition, describing him as “tested and trusted” in humanitarian service. In his remarks, Danmarke thanked the new members for joining the PDP, saying their defection reflected growing confidence in the party and his candidacy. He said the new entrants included political structures associated with a former governorship aspirant, prominent personalities, retirees and grassroots coordinators from across the state. Danmarke identified insecurity as Katsina’s most pressing challenge, pledging to make restoring security his administration’s immediate priority if elected. He also promised to revive the education, health, agriculture and infrastructure sectors, while accusing the incumbent administration of failing to meet the expectations of residents. The PDP candidate called on the people of Katsina to join what he described as the party’s movement for change, promising people-centred governance and a rebuilding of the state. The state PDP Chairman, Alhaji Nura Amadi Kurfi, gave the vote of thanks, expressing confidence that Lado’s candidacy would usher in progress and development in Katsina. The Council said the alleged attacks on opposition leaders, demolition of campaign offices, denial of campaign venues and harassment of party members were part of a coordinated effort to undermine political participation and democratic freedoms. item.title: NDLEA intercepts large consignments of illicit drugs in 7 states
item.description: The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has intercepted large consignments of illicit drugs in seven states across the country. The states include Lagos, Kano, Kaduna, Sokoto, Ondo, Oyo and Edo, in a series of intelligence-led operations. This is contained in a statement by the Director, Media and Advocacy, NDLEA, Mr Femi Babafemi on Sunday in Abuja. Breaking down the operation, Babafemi said NDLEA operatives, acting on actionable intelligence about the movement of skunk, intercepted a white Volkswagen LT 28 bus along Kudirat Abiola Way, Ikeja, Lagos. Babafemi said the NDLEA operatives intercepted 537kg of skunk, a potent strain of cannabis, on Sunday, Oct. 25, while it was being transported from the Island to the Mainland. “The same day, another team of officers intercepted a brown J5 bus along the Gbagada–Oshodi expressway, with 439 kilograms of the same substance seized,”he said. In Oyo, NDLEA operatives on Thursday conducted a follow-up operation at Idere road, Igboora, where two suspects were arrested. Babafemi said that their arrest came while loading 554 kilograms of skunk into a Volvo truck for onward movement into town. “The operation targeted a notorious drug dealer known as ‘Omo Oba’, who escaped arrest on October 25. “This happened when officers seized 309.5 kilograms of the strong cannabis strain popularly called ‘Ghanaian Loud’ linked to him,” he said. Also, in Kano, NDLEA operatives on Monday raided a location in Tsamiya area of Gezawa where they recovered 247,500 tablets of diazepam weighing 57.7 kilograms and 100,000 tablets of Exol-5 weighing 38.7 kilograms. “Two days later, on Wednesday, October 28, another team of officers stormed Dorayi area of the state, where they arrested two suspects with 19,250 pills of tramadol 225mg weighing 13.6 kilograms,” Babafemi said.
